title: The text-model garden grew
summary:
More ways to build with text models arrived alongside quieter work to make their responses, capabilities, and documentation more predictable.

The catalog gained `openai-fast` for text and image input, `openai-roblox` with tool support, and two guided personas: the in-character `mirexa` and biomimicry-focused `bidara`. The `openai` and `deepseek-reasoning` mappings were also updated. More choices are useful; knowing what each choice does is better.

Text-cache changes made completed streaming responses reusable, let equivalent requests across hosts share a cache key, and normalized headers to avoid double compression. The earlier cache rework also made requests easier to distinguish without losing streaming response types.

The `/models` endpoint gained a `tools` capability flag, and the OpenAI-compatible endpoint now forwards complete `response_format` objects, including supplied JSON schemas. `llama-vision` was removed from the available text-model list, while the Portkey mapping stopped selecting upstream models for eleven aliases, including `claude`, `gemini`, and `command-r`; that change added no replacement routing.

A Websim Worker was added to turn a prompt in a URL path into self-contained HTML, with Pollinations images and linked subpages. The MCP guides now include the community-maintained MCPollinations server, and text-to-speech POST examples show how to decode the base64 audio returned in JSON.
